name: Rehoboam
overview: Rehoboam was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Solomon who succeeded him as king. His reign marked a significant turning point in Israel's history, as he inherited the throne after Solomon's death. No additional personal notes are recorded beyond these facts.
namesAndTitles: The name Rehoboam means '[my] people will enlarge, expand,' reflecting a hopeful vision for his rule. He is also referred to by the titles 'King Rehoboam' and 'King of Judah,' indicating his royal status over the tribe of Judah after the division of the kingdom.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Rehoboam as the son of Solomon and Naamah. He was the father of Abijam and was married to Mahalath. Additionally, he had sons named Jeush, Shemariah, Zaham, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith, indicating a large family lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Rehoboam's significance lies in his role as the successor to Solomon and the first king to rule over the divided kingdom of Judah following Israel's split. His rejection of wise counsel led to the ten northern tribes breaking away, fulfilling God's judgment on Solomon's idolatry. This division shaped the biblical narrative of God's dealings with His people and set the stage for future developments in Israel's history.
